statement: For an N-dimensional random vector x ~ N(μ, Σ) partitioned as x = [x_1; x_2] with sizes [q x 1; (N - q) x 1], mean vector μ = [μ_1; μ_2], and covariance matrix Σ = [Σ_11, Σ_12; Σ_21, Σ_22], the marginal distribution of the subset x_1 is multivariate normal x_1 ~ N_q(μ_1, Σ_11), obtained by dropping the irrelevant variables x_2 from the mean vector and covariance matrix. The supplied sources contain no derivation of this result, stating only that the proof follows from the definitions of multivariate normal distributions and linear algebra.

properties.property: Any subset of components of a multivariate normal vector has a marginal distribution that is also multivariate normal.
properties.why: Extracting a subset of components can be represented as an affine transformation Y = BX using a selection matrix B, which preserves multivariate normality.

properties.property: The marginal distribution of x_1 has mean μ_1 and covariance Σ_11, distinct from the conditional distribution (x_1 | x_2 = a).
properties.why: Conditioning shifts the mean by Σ_12 Σ_22^{-1}(a - μ_2) and alters the covariance matrix to the Schur complement Σ_11 - Σ_12 Σ_22^{-1} Σ_21, whereas marginalization reflects unobserved x_2.

properties.property: Uncorrelated components of a jointly multivariate normal random vector are statistically independent.
properties.why: Zero correlation between components of a jointly normal vector implies pairwise and mutual statistical independence.

properties.property: Marginal normality of individual random variables does not imply that they are jointly multivariate normal.
properties.why: Counterexamples exist where variables are separately standard normal but their joint distribution is a mixture model rather than multivariate normal.

assumptions.assumption: The vector x has a joint multivariate normal distribution x ~ N(μ, Σ).
assumptions.breaks_when: The components are individually normal but not jointly normal (for instance, if Y = X for |X| > c and Y = -X for |X| < c).

assumptions.assumption: The matrix Σ is a valid joint covariance matrix (symmetric and positive semi-definite).
assumptions.breaks_when: Σ is asymmetric, has negative eigenvalues, or contains negative diagonal elements.

failure_modes.mode: Assuming marginal normality implies joint normality
failure_modes.signature: Linear combinations of components are not univariate normal, and joint probability calculations fail.
failure_modes.cause: Inferring joint multivariate normality solely from the fact that individual components are marginally normally distributed.

failure_modes.mode: Conflating marginal distribution with conditional distribution
failure_modes.signature: Using unadjusted marginal mean μ_1 and variance Σ_11 when a conditioning realization x_2 = a is known.
failure_modes.cause: Ignoring known observation data x_2 = a, omitting the regression term Σ_12 Σ_22^{-1}(a - μ_2) and the variance reduction from the Schur complement.

failure_modes.mode: Assuming uncorrelatedness implies independence without joint normality
failure_modes.signature: Components have zero correlation (ρ = 0) yet are statistically dependent.
failure_modes.cause: Zero correlation implies independence only under joint multivariate normality, not when variables are merely marginally normal.

instantiation.why_here: In this project, the ekf_global and ekf_local components run the robot_localization Extended Kalman Filter algorithm to estimate the robot's 15-dimensional state. The connection to Gaussian marginalization is solely that the underlying filter algorithm requires this mathematical result to propagate multivariate normal state distributions and extract marginal distributions of state subsets. The project components depend on this result because the EKF algorithm requires it, rather than exposing parameters that directly configure marginalization.

concrete.in_your_project: The full 15-dimensional robot state vector [15 x 1] estimated by ekf_global and ekf_local, comprising 3D pose, linear and angular velocities, and linear accelerations.
The dimension of the full state vector in robot_localization, which is 15 [1 x 1].
The 15-dimensional mean vector of the robot state estimate [15 x 1] maintained by the EKF.
The 15 x 15 joint state covariance matrix [15 x 15] tracking estimate uncertainties and cross-correlations across all state variables.
The subset of q state variables retained in the marginal distribution [q x 1], such as planar position or velocity components.
The dimension of the marginal subset of retained state variables [1 x 1].
The remaining (15 - q) state variables marginalized out from the full state vector [(15 - q) x 1].
The marginal mean vector for the retained subset of state variables x_1 [q x 1].
The mean vector of the marginalized state variables x_2 [(15 - q) x 1].
The marginal covariance matrix of the retained state variables x_1 [q x q], obtained by dropping unselected rows and columns from Σ.
The cross-covariance matrix between retained variables x_1 and marginalized variables x_2 [q x (15 - q)].
The cross-covariance matrix between marginalized variables x_2 and retained variables x_1 [(15 - q) x q].
The covariance matrix of the marginalized variables x_2 [(15 - q) x (15 - q)].
